title: Zuri and the Sunny Drink Warmer
markdown:
One bright morning Zuri and her robot friend Bloop hurried to the Sunny Meadow Fair. A sad sound stopped them. Coach Ellis, the snack vendor: pretzel warmer empty, water cool. “Fair-goers will expect warm drinks.”

Zuri’s mind whirred. The sky was a bright lid. She remembered how Bloop’s solar charger grew warm in the sun. “What if we used the sun’s own warmth?” She found a stout magnifying glass. Held just right, a bright beam hit a dry leaf. Snap. The leaf curled, browned, a tiny puff of smoke. “This glass makes the sunbeams strong and hot.”

“Coach Ellis — the sun’s power.”

Bloop helped carry. Ellis found shiny foil and mirrors. Zuri arranged them to catch light and aim it at the dark pot. Then the glass: a super-strong sunbeam onto the metal.

The water soaked up the rays. Soon it steamed, ready for the drinks.

Ellis cheered. “You warmed it with sunshine!”

Zuri smiled. “When we focus many beams, they make heat. Solar energy.” Bloop showed a picture of the beams meeting on the pot. Ellis poured the first cup. Zuri tested with a careful finger near the rim — warm enough — and Bloop logged the angle of the glass so the next batch would not need another leaf as a rehearsal.
